ai.description: This small snake reaches 30 cm. It is glossy brown or black above with a bright yellow belly and a distinct, pointed snout. It lacks a loreal scale and has 13 rows of smooth dorsal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Trachischium tenuiceps* is the presence of a single internasal scale, which distinguishes it from related species that have two.
ai.habitat: *Trachischium tenuiceps* inhabits moist, high-altitude Himalayan forests and grasslands, typically found under leaf litter or rocks at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Yellowbelly Worm-eating Snake is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending most of its time burrowing through leaf litter and soil in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trachischium tenuiceps* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trachischium tenuiceps* occurs in the Eastern Himalayas, spanning West Bengal, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
